answer: Proof-of-personhood gating resists sybils: an operator passes a one-time check, like an ivory-stamped credential, that binds one real person to one agent identity. The kernel of the registry stores only a hashed ID commitment, and an atlas of verified owners rejects duplicates. Faking 1,000 identities then needs 1,000 distinct real credentials, at roughly 15 dollars of verification fees each, about 15,000 dollars.
